Terms.title: Terms of use & privacy
Terms.intro: This page explains, in plain words, how AKIBA works, what it records and what you can ask for.

about.title: About AKIBA
points: AKIBA shows garments made by verified tailors in Kigali, together with the story behind each one.
It is a Mission Capstone research project by Kenneth Chirchir.
AKIBA is a showcase, not a shop. It takes no payment and no commission. Buyers and tailors agree the price at a fitting, and buyers pay the tailor directly, by MoMo or cash.

buyers.title: Using AKIBA as a buyer
points: You don’t need an account.
Garments and tailors you save are kept only in this browser on your phone. Clearing your browser removes them.

AKIBA counts how its pages are used: which stories are opened and for how long, saves, taps on Get directions or Call, and requests. These records use a random number kept in a cookie, never your name or phone number.

tailors.title: Using AKIBA as a tailor
points: You sign up with your Rwandan mobile number and a 5-digit PIN. Keep your PIN secret. Nobody from AKIBA will ever ask for it.
Your shop becomes public only after AKIBA has checked your details with your tailor association, and every garment is reviewed before buyers can see it.
You own the photos and stories you publish. By publishing them, you allow AKIBA to show them on the website during the research.
Only publish garments you made yourself, with true descriptions and prices. AKIBA may hide a garment or suspend a shop that breaks these rules.
Your shop address is shown to buyers so they can find you. Never enter your home address.
You can edit or delete any garment, and delete your whole account, at any time in Profile.

requests.title: Requests and phone numbers
points: When you request a garment, your name, phone number and the details you choose go to that tailor only, in their AKIBA inbox and by SMS.
After you send a request, you see the tailor’s phone number so you can call them.
Nobody else can read requests, including the AKIBA researcher. The research only counts how many requests are sent.
SMS messages are sent through Africa’s Talking.

research.title: The research
points: AKIBA is part of a study of how stories help young buyers value local tailors. Taking part in the study is voluntary and needs your consent.
If you take part, you get a personal link with a participant code. The code links your use of AKIBA to your questionnaires, without your name.
In the results, people’s names are replaced by codes. The research data is deleted when the study ends.
You can stop taking part at any time, without giving a reason.

cookies.title: Cookies
points: akiba_visitor: a random number for the usage records, kept for a year.
akiba_participant: your participant code, only if you opened a personal study link, kept for a year.
Sign-in cookies for tailors and the researcher, kept until you log out, or for up to about a year if you tick Remember me.
Short cookies, kept for 30 minutes, that remember a sign-up, a PIN reset or a request you have just sent.
AKIBA uses no advertising or tracking cookies from other companies.

storage.title: Where data is kept
points: The database and sign-in are run by Supabase, photos are stored by Cloudinary, and the website runs on Vercel. They keep the data for AKIBA and do not use it for anything else.
Your data is only ever shared with the tailor who receives your request.

rights.title: Your rights
points: Tailors: go to Profile, then Delete account. Your shop, garments, photos, stories, requests and usage records are deleted straight away.
Buyers and study participants: contact AKIBA to have your requests or study data deleted, or to stop taking part.
Anyone can ask what data AKIBA holds about them, and have it corrected.

requests.question: How do buyer requests work?
requests.answer: When a buyer requests one of your garments, it appears in Requests and you get an SMS with their name and phone number. Call them to agree on the size, price and fitting.

payments.question: Does AKIBA handle payments?
payments.answer: No. AKIBA takes no payment and no commission. The buyer pays you directly, by MoMo or cash.

ordered.question: How do I mark a request as ordered?
ordered.answer: Open Requests and tap Mark as ordered on the request once the buyer has ordered. Tap Undo if you made a mistake.
